title: FeGe as a building block for the kagome 1:1, 1:6:6, and 1:3:5 families: hidden d-orbital decoupling of flat band sectors, effective models and interaction Hamiltonians
authors: Y. Jiang, H. Hu, D. Calugaru, C. Felser, S. Blanco-Canosa, H. Weng, Y. Xu, B. A. Bernevig
class: loop-current (assigned) / actual: kagome multi-orbital flat-band S-matrix bipartite-lattice framework
method: Symmetry + chemistry decomposition of Fe d orbitals into 3 groups; tight-binding block Hamiltonians H = [[A, S],[S^dagger, B]] cast as generalized bipartite crystalline lattices (BCL); S-matrix (chiral) formalism for exact flat-band counting; DFT fitting; cRPA interactions. LEGO building-block extension 1:1 -> 1:6:6 -> 1:3:5.

headline_testable.statement: S-matrix / BCL flat-band counting theorem (Eq. S10.1-S10.3). For a chiral bipartite Bloch Hamiltonian H(k)=[[0_{NL}, S(k)],[S^dag(k), 0_{NLtilde}]] with NL >= NLtilde, there are at least NL - NLtilde perfectly flat bands pinned at E=0. If rank(S_k)=r_s <= NLtilde then there are NL + NLtilde - 2*r_s flat bands at zero. Adding intra-sublattice A(k) with a k-independent eigenvalue of multiplicity na>NLtilde gives na - NLtilde flat bands (energy not necessarily 0).
concrete_instances: s-orbital NN kagome (3 sites): one dispersionless flat band at E=+2t (the 'simple model' the paper argues is insufficient but which is the flat-band baseline).
H1 group d2(dx2-y2)/ptxy BCL: N_d2=3, N_p=2 -> N_d2 - N_p = 1 perfectly flat band.
Generic: rank-deficient S(k) opens extra flat bands per N_L + N_Ltilde - 2 r_s.

replication_plan: Build from-scratch numpy Bloch Hamiltonians: (a) s-orbital kagome via kagome kernel -> confirm flat band at +2t (bandwidth ~0). (b) Generic chiral bipartite H=[[0,S],[S^dag,0]] with random full-rank and rank-deficient S(k) sampled over BZ -> count zero-energy flat bands, verify = NL-NLtilde and NL+NLtilde-2rs. (c) Concrete 3+2 BCL (Nd2=3, Np=2) -> verify exactly 1 flat band at 0. Metric: number of k-independent eigenvalues (std over BZ < 1e-9).
success_criterion: Flat-band counts match theorem predictions to numerical tolerance (bandwidth < 1e-6) for all three instances.
